tasks.notes: plan-defect: M1 says simEnv sets FLEET_HOME, and the Context says sim_env() is that contract 'key for key' — but the Proof's own `Run:` for leg (h) asserts sim_env() returns no key with a FLEET_ prefix other than FLEET_TEST_SLACK, which a FLEET_HOME would fail. I resolved it in favour of the executable Run: the JS simEnv() sets FLEET_HOME (leg (a) checks only the six planted names, so it passes), and the Python sim_env() sets PATH/HOME/TMPDIR/FLEET_TEST_SLACK only. M6's own text asks only that sim_env drop the six prefixes, keep FLEET_TEST_SLACK and build PATH from the same interpreters, all of which it does. Rationale recorded in the sim_env docstring: a sim is not one of its own children, and a FLEET_ fact planted by the bridge is the ambient kind the sweep exists to keep out.

task 1: M4 enumerates nine sibling-spawn sites; I removed a tenth. test_run_main.mjs leg (f) shelled out to `sh -c "node fleet/tests/test_roles_peer.mjs | grep -q 'ALL TESTS PASSED'"` and the same for test_exam_edited_patches.mjs. The task's own discovery grep (`(spawnSync|execFileSync|execFile|spawn)\((process\.execPath|'node')`) cannot see a sim named inside a shell string, so it missed them — but M4's categorical claim and the Proof's `Run:` grep (`(spawn|...)\([^;]*(test_[a-z_]*\.mjs|pytest)`) both catch them, so they had to go. Replaced by an fs.existsSync loop over the two names, leg letter and citation kept. test_run_main.mjs is in FILES, so this is inside the footprint.

task 1: The probe's static sweep must distinguish `child_process` spawn calls from regex `.exec(` calls and from the lobby/janitor/launch sims' own `exec` seam functions — there are ~40 such non-spawn `exec(` sites across the tree. The task text defines a spawn site as 'a call to one of the six child_process names', which I read as requiring the sweep to resolve the name to a node:child_process import; a sweep that matched the bare token `exec(` would name dozens of false offenders. My own verification sweep resolved the imported names per file and found zero spawns without a simEnv-derived env.

task 1: examiner: (h) [M6] — the planted-key `python3 -c` Run: prints an empty `bad` list, FLEET_TEST_SLACK comes back as `7`, and every returned PATH entry is a directory holding one of node/python3/git/bash/sh — That half is an execution of the bridge's sim_env() in a planted process, and the probe spawns nothing by leg (f)/M7 — it imports no child_process at all, so it cannot run python3 without failing its own leg. Encoded statically instead: the exam asserts tests/test_fleet_suite.py declares a module-level sim_env() whose body names all six dropped prefixes, FLEET_TEST_SLACK, the five interpreters and HOME/TMPDIR/FLEET_HOME, and that subprocess.run(["node", path], …) binds env=sim_env(). The executable half is the task's own `Run:` line.

task 1: examiner: (i) [M5] — under the planted `xargs` Run:, every file `ls fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot*.mjs` lists runs directly under node with TINYAPP_RENDER_URL/FLEET_RENDER_ENV planted and prints the sentinel, so xargs exits 0 — Same reason: running the boot sims under a plant is a spawn, and the probe spawns nothing (leg (f)/M7). Encoded statically instead: the exam pins /etc/fleet/render.env to exactly one line of fleet/sandbox-boot.sh and that line to `FLEET_RENDER_ENV="${FLEET_RENDER_ENV:-/etc/fleet/render.env}"`, and pins the rig's bootEnv to bind FLEET_RENDER_ENV: renderEnvPath( under the case's home. The executable half is the task's own `Run:` line.
